paper_metadata.title: Effect of Low Temperatures on Mechanical and Physical Properties of High-Strength Nickel Alloy ÉK61-ID and Stainless Maraging Steel ÉK49-VD

evidence.quote: The Énergomash RPA traditionally uses nickel-base alloys for the piping and units operating in oxygen in any temperature range (including the cryogenic one).
The high-strength low-carbon stainless steel ÉK49-VD is widely used for operation at cryogenic temperatures up to 20 K (liquid hydrogen).
Elastic seals of DJ operating in liquid oxygen are produced from high-strength nickel alloy ÉK61-ID.

evidence.quote: Low-carbon maraging steels are well weldable and do not require heat treatment after the welding
The low-carbon martensite of steel ÉK49-VD has a high ductility at cryogenic temperatures up to 20 K
the structure of low-carbon maraging steels has a twice-lower amount of retained austenite than the austenitic-martensitic steels
metallic alloys of the austenitic class are preferable for operation at cryogenic temperatures

The tests of DJ simulators with seals from steel ÉK49-VD in liquid hydrogen at a pressure of 35 MPa under conditions close to actual ones showed that the seal provided a high tightness. The leakage did not exceed about 7.5 × 10 –1 1 g/sec
they possess enhanced fracture toughness due to the cobalt additive that decreases the cold-shortness threshold
